name: The state (ḥāl)
definition: A noun in naṣb that tells the state of a person or thing at the time of the act.
body: Jāʾa zaydun rākiban: Zayd came riding. The ḥāl answers 'in what state?'. Al-Ājurrūmiyya: it is always indefinite, comes only after a complete sentence, and the one whose state it tells (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) is mostly definite.
It differs from the naʿt: al-rākibu after zaydun would describe Zayd always; rākiban tells only how he came.
